name: export
description: Marks shell variables for export to child processes, making them environment variables.

flags.description: Set the variable in the current shell only.
Set AND export to child processes.

examples.explanation: Programs launched from this shell (git, crontab -e) now open vim.
Exports a variable — child scripts can read it as $API_KEY. Note: this lands in shell history.
Alternative one-shot form: the variable exists ONLY for that command, never entering the shell or history.
Appends to PATH. Always include the existing $PATH — overwriting it breaks every command lookup.

about: A plain variable lives only in the current shell; an exported one is copied into the environment of every child process. Environment is inherited downward only — a child can never modify the parent's variables, which is why scripts cannot "export back" to your shell (use source for that).
useCases: Extend PATH with personal bin directories.
mistakes: Forgetting export and wondering why a script cannot see the variable.
Overwriting PATH instead of appending ($PATH: missing).
warnings: Secrets exported in ~/.bashrc or typed on the command line persist in files and shell history — prefer secret managers or per-command env for sensitive values.
